subject: math
title: 12- and 24-Hour Time: Analog Clocks, a.m. and p.m., and Schedules
seo_title: Grade 4 Math: 12- and 24-Hour Time Worksheets (Free, BC Curriculum, Answer Key)
standard_text: How to tell time with analog and digital clocks, using 12- and 24-hour clocks
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 math worksheets on telling time for the BC curriculum: read analog clocks to the minute, match analog and digital clocks, use a.m. and p.m., convert between 12-hour and 24-hour time, and work out elapsed time with ferry and SkyTrain schedules. 100 questions with an answer key, good numeracy practice for the FSA.
key_big: p.m.: add 12 to the hour. 3:45 p.m. = 15:45.
key_sub: To go back, take away 12: 15:00 is 3:00 p.m., not 5:00 p.m. Just after midnight is 00 (12:30 a.m. = 00:30). An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so count on to the next o’clock when you work out how long.
body_html:
Reading an analog clock to the minute

The short hand shows the hour. The long hand shows the minutes. Each number is 5 minutes for the long hand, and each small mark is 1 minute. Count by 5s to the last number, then count on by 1s.

a.m. and p.m.

A day has 24 hours, but a clock face shows only 12. In 12-hour time we write a.m. for times from midnight to noon (night and morning) and p.m. for times from noon to midnight (afternoon and evening).

a.m. or p.m.?

Simran eats dinner at 22 minutes to 6 in the evening. Write the time.

22 minutes to 6 is 38 minutes past 5. It is the evening, so it is p.m.

Answer: 5:38 p.m.

24-hour time

The 24-hour clock counts the hours from 00 to 23, so it needs no a.m. or p.m. It always has 4 digits: 07:30, 15:45. Ferry and transit schedules often use it.

12-hour24-hourRule
7:30 a.m.07:30a.m.: keep the hour, write 4 digits
12:15 p.m.12:15just after noon: keep 12
3:45 p.m.15:45p.m.: add 12 (3 + 12 = 15)
9:10 p.m.21:10p.m.: add 12 (9 + 12 = 21)
12:30 a.m.00:30just after midnight: 00

To go back to 12-hour time, take away 12 from the hours 13 to 23: 18:05 is 18 − 12 = 6, so 6:05 p.m.

24-hour to 12-hour

Write 15:00 as a 12-hour time.

15 − 12 = 3. The hour is after 12, so it is p.m.

Answer: 3:00 p.m.

Elapsed time: how long?

An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not subtract times like ordinary numbers. Jump to the next o’clock first, then on to the end time.

Read a ferry schedule

A ferry leaves Tsawwassen at 13:00 and arrives at Swartz Bay at 14:35. How long is the crossing?

13:00 to 14:00 is 1 hour. 14:00 to 14:35 is 35 minutes.

Answer: 1 hour 35 minutes

Find the end time

Hockey practice starts at 17:45 and lasts 1 hour 20 minutes. When does it end?

17:45 + 1 hour = 18:45. 18:45 + 15 minutes = 19:00, then 5 more minutes.

Answer: 19:05

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
15:00 read as 5:00 p.m.Take away 12, do not just drop the 1. 15 − 12 = 3, so 3:00 p.m.
3:45 p.m. written as 13:45 or 03:45p.m.: add 12 to the hour. 3 + 12 = 15, so 15:45
12:30 a.m. written as 12:30Just after midnight is 00 in 24-hour time: 00:30
Swapping the hands: reading 4:38 as 7:20The short hand is the hour. The long hand is the minutes
Short hand just before 5 read as 5:38The short hand has not reached 5 yet, so the hour is still 4: 4:38
15:52 to 16:09 worked out as 1609 − 1552 = 57 minutesAn hour has 60 minutes, not 100. Count on: 8 + 9 = 17 minutes

faq.q: What do Grade 4 students learn about time in BC?
faq.a: In the BC Grade 4 math curriculum, students learn how to tell time with analog and digital clocks, using both 12-hour and 24-hour clocks. Using a.m. and p.m. and working out how long events last are a natural part of this.

faq.q: How do you change 24-hour time to 12-hour time?
faq.a: For hours from 13 to 23, take away 12 and write p.m. (15:45 is 3:45 p.m.). For hours from 01 to 11, keep the hour and write a.m. (08:15 is 8:15 a.m.). 12:00 is noon and 00:00 is midnight.

faq.q: Is 00:30 in the morning or at night?
faq.a: 00:30 is 12:30 a.m., which is 30 minutes after midnight, in the middle of the night. 12:30 in the afternoon is written 12:30 in 24-hour time.

faq.q: Is telling time on the Grade 4 FSA?
faq.a: The Foundation Skills Assessment (FSA) that BC students write in Grade 4 checks numeracy skills from the BC curriculum, and it does not list every topic in advance. Reading clocks, 24-hour time and schedules is good all-round numeracy practice.

sets.title: Reading analog clocks to the minute

items.e: The short hour hand is between 3 and 4. It has not reached 4 yet, so the hour is 3. The long minute hand points to 2. Count by 5s: 2 × 5 = 10 minutes. So the time is 3:10. (Not 2:15: that swaps the hands. The short hand is the hour.)

The short hour hand is between 7 and 8. It has not reached 8 yet, so the hour is 7. The long minute hand points to 5. Count by 5s: 5 × 5 = 25 minutes. So the time is 7:25. (Not 5:35: that swaps the hands. The short hand is the hour.)

The short hour hand is between 9 and 10. It has not reached 10 yet, so the hour is 9. The long minute hand points to 8. Count by 5s: 8 × 5 = 40 minutes. So the time is 9:40. (Not 10:40: the hour hand has not reached 10 yet.)

The short hour hand is between 6 and 7. It has not reached 7 yet, so the hour is 6. The long minute hand points to 11. Count by 5s: 11 × 5 = 55 minutes. So the time is 6:55. (Not 7:55: the hour hand has not reached 7 yet.)

The short hour hand is between 2 and 3. It has not reached 3 yet, so the hour is 2. The long minute hand is 4 small marks past the 12: 4 minutes. So the time is 2:04. (Not 12:10: that swaps the hands. The short hand is the hour.)

The short hour hand is between 11 and 12. It has not reached 12 yet, so the hour is 11. The long minute hand is 4 small marks past the 2. Count by 5s to 10, then by 1s: 14 minutes. So the time is 11:14. (Not 11:10: count the small marks after the 2 too.)

The short hour hand is between 1 and 2. It has not reached 2 yet, so the hour is 1. The long minute hand is 3 small marks past the 3. Count by 5s to 15, then by 1s: 18 minutes. So the time is 1:18. (Not 1:15: count the small marks after the 3 too.)

The short hour hand is between 5 and 6. It has not reached 6 yet, so the hour is 5. The long minute hand is 4 small marks past the 4. Count by 5s to 20, then by 1s: 24 minutes. So the time is 5:24. (Not 5:20: count the small marks after the 4 too.)

The short hour hand is between 10 and 11. It has not reached 11 yet, so the hour is 10. The long minute hand is 2 small marks past the 6. Count by 5s to 30, then by 1s: 32 minutes. So the time is 10:32. (Not 11:32: the hour hand has not reached 11 yet.)

The short hour hand is between 6 and 7. It has not reached 7 yet, so the hour is 6. The long minute hand is 4 small marks past the 7. Count by 5s to 35, then by 1s: 39 minutes. So the time is 6:39. (Not 7:39: the hour hand has not reached 7 yet.)

The short hour hand is between 11 and 12. It has not reached 12 yet, so the hour is 11. The long minute hand is 1 small mark past the 8. Count by 5s to 40, then by 1s: 41 minutes. So the time is 11:41. (Not 12:41: the hour hand has not reached 12 yet.)

The short hour hand is between 12 and 1. It has not reached 1 yet, so the hour is 12. The long minute hand is 1 small mark past the 9. Count by 5s to 45, then by 1s: 46 minutes. So the time is 12:46. (Not 1:46: the hour hand has not reached 1 yet.)

The short hour hand is between 2 and 3. It has not reached 3 yet, so the hour is 2. The long minute hand is 2 small marks past the 10. Count by 5s to 50, then by 1s: 52 minutes. So the time is 2:52. (Not 3:52: the hour hand has not reached 3 yet.)

The short hour hand is between 3 and 4. It has not reached 4 yet, so the hour is 3. The long minute hand is 4 small marks past the 11. Count by 5s to 55, then by 1s: 59 minutes. So the time is 3:59. (Not 4:59: the hour hand has not reached 4 yet.)

The short hour hand is between 11 and 12. It has not reached 12 yet, so the hour is 11. The long minute hand is 3 small marks past the 4. Count by 5s to 20, then by 1s: 23 minutes. The long hand is on the right side of the clock, so we say past 11: 23 minutes past 11.

The short hour hand is between 8 and 9. It has not reached 9 yet, so the hour is 8. The long minute hand is 2 small marks past the 7. Count by 5s to 35, then by 1s: 37 minutes. That is after half past, so count the minutes to the next hour: 60 − 37 = 23. It is 23 minutes to 9. (Not “to 8”: 8 o’clock has already passed.)

The short hour hand is between 6 and 7. It has not reached 7 yet, so the hour is 6. The long minute hand is 2 small marks past the 9. Count by 5s to 45, then by 1s: 47 minutes. That is after half past, so count the minutes to the next hour: 60 − 47 = 13. It is 13 minutes to 7. (Not “to 6”: 6 o’clock has already passed.)

The short hour hand is between 3 and 4. It has not reached 4 yet, so the hour is 3. The long minute hand is 2 small marks past the 7. Count by 5s to 35, then by 1s: 37 minutes. It is 3:37. An hour has 60 minutes, so there are 60 − 37 = 23 minutes until 4 o’clock. (Not 63: an hour is 60 minutes, not 100.)

The short hour hand is between 1 and 2. It has not reached 2 yet, so the hour is 1. The long minute hand is 3 small marks past the 9. Count by 5s to 45, then by 1s: 48 minutes. It is 1:48. An hour has 60 minutes, so there are 60 − 48 = 12 minutes until 2 o’clock. (Not 52: an hour is 60 minutes, not 100.)

The short hour hand is between 8 and 9. It has not reached 9 yet, so the hour is 8. The long minute hand is 3 small marks past the 10. Count by 5s to 50, then by 1s: 53 minutes. It is 8:53. An hour has 60 minutes, so there are 60 − 53 = 7 minutes until 9 o’clock. (Not 47: an hour is 60 minutes, not 100.)

items.q: Write quarter past 10 as a digital time.
items.e: Quarter past means 15 minutes after the hour. So quarter past 10 is 10:15.

items.q: How do we say this digital time in words?
items.e: 4:20 is 20 minutes after 4 o’clock. It is before half past, so say past: 20 past 4.

items.q: How do we say this digital time in words?
items.e: 8:45 is 45 minutes past 8. 60 − 45 = 15, and 15 minutes is a quarter of an hour. So it is quarter to 9.

At 3:47 the long hand is 2 small marks past the 9 (47 minutes), and the short hand is between 3 and 4. That is clock A. Not the others: clock B shows 2:47 (its hour hand is between 2 and 3); clock C shows 3:13; clock D has the hands swapped (9:15).

items.q: The digital clock shows this time. Where is the short hour hand on an analog clock?
items.e: At 2:14 only 14 minutes have passed since 2 o’clock. The hour hand has moved only a little past 2: just past 2. It points exactly on 2 only at 2:00.

items.q: Where does the long minute hand point on an analog clock?
items.e: Count by 5s to the 4: 4 × 5 = 20. Then count on by 1s: 3 more makes 23. So the long hand is 3 small marks past the 4. (Not 3 small marks past the 2: the numbers on a clock count by 5s, so you cannot read the digits 2 and 3 separately.)

items.q: Write 20 to 6 as a digital time.
items.e: “20 to 6” means 20 minutes before 6 o’clock. 60 − 20 = 40, so it is 40 minutes past 5: 5:40. (Not 6:20: that is 20 minutes after 6 o’clock.)

items.q: The digital clock shows this time. Where is the short hour hand on an analog clock?
items.e: At 10:30 it is half past 10. The hour hand has gone half of the way from 10 to 11: halfway between 10 and 11.

At 9:17 the long hand is 2 small marks past the 3 (17 minutes), and the short hand is between 9 and 10. That is clock D. Not the others: clock A shows 8:17 (its hour hand is between 8 and 9); clock B shows 9:43; clock C has the hands swapped (3:45).

items.q: Where does the long minute hand point on an analog clock?
items.e: Count by 5s to the 3: 3 × 5 = 15. Then count on by 1s: 1 more makes 16. So the long hand is 1 small mark past the 3. (Not 6 small marks past the 1: the numbers on a clock count by 5s, so you cannot read the digits 1 and 6 separately.)

items.q: How do we say this digital time in words?
items.e: 2:51 is 51 minutes past 2. That is after half past, so say to the next hour. 60 − 51 = 9, so it is 9 minutes to 3. (Not “to 2”: 2 o’clock has already passed.)

items.q: Write 27 minutes to 2 as a digital time.
items.e: “27 minutes to 2” means 27 minutes before 2 o’clock. 60 − 27 = 33, so it is 33 minutes past 1: 1:33. (Not 2:27: that is 27 minutes after 2 o’clock.)

At 6:53 the long hand is 3 small marks past the 10 (53 minutes), and the short hand is between 6 and 7. That is clock C. Not the others: clock A shows 5:53 (its hour hand is between 5 and 6); clock B shows 6:07; clock D has the hands swapped (10:30).

items.q: The digital clock shows this time. Where is the short hour hand on an analog clock?
items.e: At 7:48 it is 12 minutes to 8. The hour hand is almost at 8, but it has not reached it: just before 8. (It is still 7 o’clock and something, so the digital time starts with 7.)

items.q: Where does the long minute hand point on an analog clock?
items.e: Count by 5s to the 9: 9 × 5 = 45. Then count on by 1s: 3 more makes 48. So the long hand is 3 small marks past the 9. (Not 8 small marks past the 4: the numbers on a clock count by 5s, so you cannot read the digits 4 and 8 separately.)

items.q: How do we say this digital time in words?
items.e: 7:36 is 36 minutes past 7. That is after half past, so say to the next hour. 60 − 36 = 24, so it is 24 minutes to 8. (Not “to 7”: 7 o’clock has already passed.)

items.q: Write 8 minutes to 12 as a digital time.
items.e: “8 minutes to 12” means 8 minutes before 12 o’clock. 60 − 8 = 52, so it is 52 minutes past 11: 11:52. (Not 12:08: that is 8 minutes after 12 o’clock.)

At 11:08 the long hand is 3 small marks past the 1 (8 minutes), and the short hand is between 11 and 12. That is clock B. Not the others: clock A shows 10:08 (its hour hand is between 10 and 11); clock C shows 11:52; clock D has the hands swapped (1:55).

items.q: The digital clock shows this time. Where is the short hour hand on an analog clock?
items.e: At 4:53 it is 7 minutes to 5. The hour hand is almost at 5, but it has not reached it: just before 5. (It is still 4 o’clock and something, so the digital time starts with 4.)

items.q: Where does the long minute hand point on an analog clock?
items.e: Count by 5s to the 7: 7 × 5 = 35. Then count on by 1s: 2 more makes 37. So the long hand is 2 small marks past the 7. (Not 7 small marks past the 3: the numbers on a clock count by 5s, so you cannot read the digits 3 and 7 separately.)
a.m. times go from midnight to noon (night and morning). p.m. times go from noon to midnight (afternoon and evening).
The afternoon is after noon, so it is a p.m. time. 3:20 a.m. is in the middle of the night. So the answer is 3:20 p.m.

items.q: Ethan eats breakfast at 7:25 in the morning. Is that a.m. or p.m.?
c: a.m., because it is after noon
a.m., because it is before noon
p.m., because it is after noon
p.m., because it is before noon
items.e: Morning times are before noon. Times before noon are a.m. times. So breakfast is at 7:25 a.m.

c: 12 o’clock in the middle of the day
the time the sun goes down
items.e: Midnight is 12 o’clock at night, when one day ends and the next day starts. 12 o’clock in the middle of the day is noon.

items.q: Which is a sensible time for school to start?
items.e: School starts in the morning, so it is an a.m. time. 3:40 a.m. is the middle of the night. So it is 8:40 a.m.

items.q: Which is a sensible time for the summer fireworks at English Bay in Vancouver?
items.e: Fireworks need a dark sky, so they are late in the evening: a p.m. time. 10:00 a.m. is in the morning. So it is 10:00 p.m.

The short hour hand is between 2 and 3. It has not reached 3 yet, so the hour is 2. The long minute hand is 3 small marks past the 7. Count by 5s to 35, then by 1s: 38 minutes. It is after noon, so it is p.m. So the time is 2:38 p.m. (Not 2:38 a.m.: that is in the middle of the night.)

The short hour hand is between 4 and 5. It has not reached 5 yet, so the hour is 4. The long minute hand is 1 small mark past the 5. Count by 5s to 25, then by 1s: 26 minutes. It is after noon, so it is p.m. So the time is 4:26 p.m. (Not 4:26 a.m.: that is in the middle of the night.)

items.q: Which is a sensible time for a Saturday morning ski lesson on Grouse Mountain?
items.e: A morning lesson is before noon, so it is an a.m. time. 2:30 a.m. and 12:30 a.m. are in the middle of the night. So it is 9:30 a.m.

The short hour hand is between 5 and 6. It has not reached 6 yet, so the hour is 5. The long minute hand is 4 small marks past the 8. Count by 5s to 40, then by 1s: 44 minutes. It is in the morning, so it is a.m. So the time is 5:44 a.m. (Not 5:44 p.m.: that is in the afternoon or evening.)

The short hour hand is between 8 and 9. It has not reached 9 yet, so the hour is 8. The long minute hand is 4 small marks past the 1. Count by 5s to 5, then by 1s: 9 minutes. It is after noon, so it is p.m. So the time is 8:09 p.m. (Not 8:09 a.m.: that is in the morning.)

items.q: Which is a sensible time for school to end?
items.e: School ends in the afternoon, after noon, so it is a p.m. time. 2:55 a.m. is in the middle of the night. So it is 2:55 p.m.

The short hour hand is between 12 and 1. It has not reached 1 yet, so the hour is 12. The long minute hand is 4 small marks past the 1. Count by 5s to 5, then by 1s: 9 minutes. It is after noon, so it is p.m. So the time is 12:09 p.m. (Not 12:09 a.m.: that is in the middle of the night.)

items.q: Which time is earliest in the day?
items.e: a.m. times come before noon and p.m. times come after noon. So 11:45 a.m. is the earliest, even though 11 is a bigger number than 1 or 2.

The short hour hand is between 10 and 11. It has not reached 11 yet, so the hour is 10. The long minute hand is 2 small marks past the 8. Count by 5s to 40, then by 1s: 42 minutes. It is in the morning, so it is a.m. So the time is 10:42 a.m. (Not 10:42 p.m.: that is late at night.)

The short hour hand is between 6 and 7. It has not reached 7 yet, so the hour is 6. The long minute hand is 3 small marks past the 9. Count by 5s to 45, then by 1s: 48 minutes. It is after noon, so it is p.m. So the time is 6:48 p.m. (Not 6:48 a.m.: that is in the morning.)

items.q: Put these times in order from earliest to latest in one day: 4:00 p.m., 6:30 a.m., 9:15 p.m., 10:00 a.m.
items.e: All a.m. times come first, then the p.m. times. a.m.: 6:30, then 10:00. p.m.: 4:00, then 9:15. So the order is 6:30 a.m., 10:00 a.m., 4:00 p.m., 9:15 p.m.

The short hour hand is between 8 and 9. It has not reached 9 yet, so the hour is 8. The long minute hand is 1 small mark past the 2. Count by 5s to 10, then by 1s: 11 minutes. It is in the morning, so it is a.m. So the time is 8:11 a.m. (Not 8:11 p.m.: that is in the afternoon or evening.)

items.q: How many hours is it from 10:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m.?
items.e: 10:00 a.m. → 12:00 noon is 2 hours. 12:00 noon → 3:00 p.m. is 3 hours. 2 + 3 = 5 hours. (Not 7: 10 − 3 = 7 does not work across noon. Not 6: count the jumps, not the numbers.)

items.q: How many hours is it from 8:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. the next morning?
items.e: 8:00 p.m. → 12:00 midnight is 4 hours. Midnight → 6:00 a.m. is 6 hours. 4 + 6 = 10 hours. (Not 2: 8 − 6 = 2 does not work across midnight.)
p.m. times are after noon. Add 12 to the hour: 3 + 12 = 15. So 3:45 p.m. is 15:45. (Not 03:45: that would be a morning time.)
a.m. times are before noon, so the hour stays the same. A 24-hour time has 4 digits, so put a 0 in front: 7:30 a.m. is 07:30. (Not 19:30: that is in the evening.)
p.m. times are after noon. Add 12 to the hour: 1 + 12 = 13. So 1:20 p.m. is 13:20. (Not 01:20: that would be a morning time.)
Hours from 13 to 23 are p.m. times. Take away 12: 15 − 12 = 3. So 15:00 is 3:00 p.m. (Not 5:00 p.m.: do not just drop the 1. 15 − 12 = 3, not 5.)
p.m. times are after noon. Add 12 to the hour: 6 + 12 = 18. So 6:05 p.m. is 18:05. (Not 06:05: that would be a morning time.)
a.m. times are before noon, so the hour stays the same. A 24-hour time has 4 digits, so put a 0 in front: 9:52 a.m. is 09:52. (Not 21:52: that is in the evening.)
The hour 08 is less than 12, so it is a morning time: a.m. Drop the 0 at the front: 8:15 a.m. (Not 8:15 p.m.: only hours from 12 to 23 are p.m.)
Hours from 13 to 23 are p.m. times. Take away 12: 17 − 12 = 5. So 17:25 is 5:25 p.m. (Not 7:25 p.m.: do not just drop the 1. 17 − 12 = 5, not 7.)
Hours from 13 to 23 are p.m. times. Take away 12: 14 − 12 = 2. So 14:10 is 2:10 p.m. (Not 4:10 p.m.: do not just drop the 1. 14 − 12 = 2, not 4.)
p.m. times are after noon. Add 12 to the hour: 9 + 12 = 21. So 9:38 p.m. is 21:38. (Not 09:38: that would be a morning time.)
Hours from 13 to 23 are p.m. times. Take away 12: 19 − 12 = 7. So 19:47 is 7:47 p.m. (Not 9:47 p.m.: do not just drop the 1. 19 − 12 = 7, not 9.)
Hours from 13 to 23 are p.m. times. 19 − 12 = 7, so 19:30 is 7:30 p.m., in the evening. 07:30, 09:30 and 11:30 are all a.m. times. The answer is 19:30.
00 is the hour just after midnight. In 12-hour time we call it 12 a.m. So 00:30 is 12:30 a.m., 30 minutes after midnight. (12:30 p.m. is 30 minutes after noon.)
12:20 a.m. is 20 minutes after midnight. In 24-hour time, the hour after midnight is 00. So it is 00:20. (12:20 is 20 minutes after noon.)
12:45 p.m. is 45 minutes after noon. Noon is 12:00 in 24-hour time, so do not add 12. It is 12:45.

The short hour hand is between 8 and 9. It has not reached 9 yet, so the hour is 8. The long minute hand points to 5. Count by 5s: 5 × 5 = 25 minutes. It is 8:25 in the evening, so it is 8:25 p.m. Add 12 to the hour: 8 + 12 = 20. So it is 20:25.

The short hour hand is between 1 and 2. It has not reached 2 yet, so the hour is 1. The long minute hand is 2 small marks past the 10. Count by 5s to 50, then by 1s: 52 minutes. It is 1:52 in the afternoon, so it is 1:52 p.m. Add 12 to the hour: 1 + 12 = 13. So it is 13:52.
The short hand is between 5 and 6, so it is 5:40 p.m. In the afternoon, read the green number next to the 5: 17. So it is 17:40. (Not 18:40: the hour hand has not reached 6, or 18, yet.)

The short hour hand is between 10 and 11. It has not reached 11 yet, so the hour is 10. The long minute hand is 1 small mark past the 2. Count by 5s to 10, then by 1s: 11 minutes. It is 10:11 at night, so it is 10:11 p.m. Add 12 to the hour: 10 + 12 = 22. So it is 22:11.

items.q: Which 24-hour time is quarter to 4 in the afternoon?
items.e: Quarter to 4 is 15 minutes before 4:00, so it is 3:45 p.m. Add 12 to the hour: 3 + 12 = 15. It is 15:45. (Not 16:45: quarter to 4 is before 4 o’clock.)

items.q: Recess starts at 10:10 a.m. and ends at 10:25 a.m. How long is recess?
items.e: Both times are in the same hour. 25 − 10 = 15 minutes.

items.q: Noah’s hockey practice is from 6:15 a.m. to 7:30 a.m. How long is practice?
items.e: 6:15 to 7:15 is 1 hour. 7:15 to 7:30 is 15 minutes. So practice is 1 hour 15 minutes. (Not 115 minutes: 730 − 615 = 115 treats an hour as 100 minutes.)

items.q: Lunch starts at 11:40 a.m. and ends at 12:20 p.m. How long is lunch?
items.e: Count on to 12:00 noon first: 11:40 a.m. to 12:00 is 20 minutes. Then 12:00 to 12:20 p.m. is 20 minutes. 20 + 20 = 40 minutes. (Not 80: 1220 − 1140 = 80 treats an hour as 100 minutes.)

items.q: Owen gets on the SkyTrain at Waterfront Station at 15:52. He gets off at Metrotown at 16:09. How long is the ride?
items.e: Count on to the next hour first: 15:52 to 16:00 is 8 minutes. Then 16:00 to 16:09 is 9 minutes. 8 + 9 = 17 minutes. (Not 57: 1609 − 1552 = 57 treats an hour as 100 minutes.)

items.q: The ferry leaves Tsawwassen at 11:00. What time does it arrive at Swartz Bay?
items.e: Find 11:00 in the “Leaves Tsawwassen” column. Look across that row: it arrives at 12:35. (10:35 and 14:35 are on other rows.)

items.q: How long does the ferry take to go from Tsawwassen to Swartz Bay?
items.e: Take any row, such as 11:00 to 12:35. 11:00 to 12:00 is 1 hour. 12:00 to 12:35 is 35 minutes. So the crossing takes 1 hour 35 minutes. (Not 135 minutes: 1235 − 1100 = 135 treats an hour as 100 minutes. 1 hour 35 minutes is 95 minutes.)

items.q: A lacrosse practice lasts 90 minutes. How long is that in hours and minutes?
items.e: 60 minutes make 1 hour. 90 − 60 = 30 minutes left over. So 90 minutes = 1 hour 30 minutes. (1 hour 10 minutes would be 70 minutes.)

items.q: A hockey practice starts at 17:45. It lasts 1 hour 20 minutes. What time does it end?
items.e: Add 1 hour: 17:45 → 18:45. Then add 20 minutes: 15 minutes takes you to 19:00, and 5 more makes 19:05. (Not 19:25: that adds 1 hour 40 minutes.)

items.q: Mei’s hockey practice starts at 6:15 a.m. She leaves home 35 minutes before. What time does she leave home?
items.e: Count back 15 minutes to 6:00 a.m. 35 − 15 = 20, so count back 20 more minutes: 5:40 a.m. (6:50 a.m. is 35 minutes after 6:15.)

items.q: Sofia arrives at Swartz Bay at 4:35 p.m. Which sailing did she take from Tsawwassen?
items.e: 4:35 p.m. in 24-hour time is 4 + 12 = 16, so 16:35. Find 16:35 in the “Arrives” column. That ferry leaves Tsawwassen at 15:00. (Not 13:00: that ferry arrives at 14:35, which is 2:35 p.m.)

items.q: A hockey game on TV starts at 19:00 and ends at 21:40. How long is it?
items.e: 19:00 to 21:00 is 2 hours. 21:00 to 21:40 is 40 minutes. So the game is 2 hours 40 minutes. (Count the jumps 19 → 20 → 21: that is 2 hours, not 3. Not 240 minutes: 2140 − 1900 = 240 treats an hour as 100 minutes.)

items.q: A SkyTrain leaves Waterfront at 08:47. The ride to King George Station takes 39 minutes. What time does it get there?
items.e: From 08:47, 13 minutes takes you to 09:00. 39 − 13 = 26 more minutes makes 09:26. (Not 08:26: going past 60 minutes means the hour goes up by 1.)

items.q: Kai’s family must be at Swartz Bay by 7:00 p.m. What is the latest ferry they can take from Tsawwassen?
items.e: 7:00 p.m. is 19:00. Look down the “Arrives” column for the last time before 19:00: 18:35. That ferry leaves at 17:00. (The 19:00 ferry leaves at 7:00 p.m., so it arrives too late. 18:35 is an arrival time, not a sailing.)

items.q: The class field trip bus leaves for Stanley Park at 09:15. It gets back to school at 14:40. How long is the trip?
items.e: 09:15 to 14:15 is 5 hours (10, 11, 12, 13, 14). 14:15 to 14:40 is 25 minutes. So the trip is 5 hours 25 minutes.

items.q: Liam gets to the Tsawwassen terminal at 13:20, just after the 13:00 ferry has left. How long must he wait for the next ferry?
items.e: The next ferry is at 15:00. 13:20 to 14:00 is 40 minutes. 14:00 to 15:00 is 1 hour. So the wait is 1 hour 40 minutes. (Not 1 hour 80 minutes: 1500 − 1320 = 180 treats an hour as 100 minutes.)

items.q: The ferry from Horseshoe Bay to Nanaimo leaves at 10:40. The crossing takes 1 hour 40 minutes. What time does it arrive?
items.e: Add 1 hour: 10:40 → 11:40. Then add 40 minutes: 20 minutes takes you to 12:00, and 20 more makes 12:20. (Not 12:40: that adds 2 hours.)

items.q: Zara’s family drives up the Sea-to-Sky Highway to Whistler. They leave at 7:50 a.m. and arrive at 9:35 a.m. How long is the drive?
items.e: 7:50 to 8:00 is 10 minutes. 8:00 to 9:00 is 1 hour. 9:00 to 9:35 is 35 minutes. 10 + 35 = 45, so the drive is 1 hour 45 minutes. (Not 185 minutes: 935 − 750 = 185 treats an hour as 100 minutes.)

items.q: Harjot’s swimming lesson lasts 1 hour 15 minutes. Simran’s lesson lasts 80 minutes. Whose lesson is longer, and by how much?
items.e: 1 hour 15 minutes = 60 + 15 = 75 minutes. 80 − 75 = 5. So Simran’s lesson is longer, by 5 minutes. (Not Harjot’s by 35: that counts an hour as 100 minutes.)

items.q: The school Terry Fox Run starts at 10:30 a.m. Ava finishes at 11:12 a.m. How long does she take?
items.e: 10:30 to 11:00 is 30 minutes. 11:00 to 11:12 is 12 minutes. 30 + 12 = 42 minutes. (Not 82: 1112 − 1030 = 82 treats an hour as 100 minutes.)

items.q: Mateo’s family takes the 13:00 ferry from Tsawwassen. The crossing takes 1 hour 35 minutes. Then they drive 30 minutes to Victoria. What time do they get to Victoria in 12-hour time?
